speakers.name: Salmaan Allibhai
speakers.title: Chief Actuary and head of data and analytics

exchanges.question: Can you expand on new business quotes and bind order trends year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter and how these compare to submission growth? Given your expense ratio advantage and returns, will Kinsale deteriorate accident year loss ratio for higher growth?
exchanges.answer: New disclosure provided due to requests for more granular information; but more granular metrics are more volatile in 90-day periods. Across 25 divisions shows plenty of opportunities in some, more competition in others. Company manages all product lines to low 20s ROE or greater, constantly adjusting pricing; Q1 ROE was 24%, no meaningful deterioration expected.

exchanges.question: Accident year loss ratio much better than expected, up 40 basis points year-over-year—any one-offs or favorable weather? E&S Homeowners declined 22% in quarter—competition or timing? On reinsurance renewal, with below-average hurricane forecast but lower reinsurance costs, how thinking about retentions?
exchanges.responderTitle: Chief Actuary and head of data and analytics
exchanges.answer: Nothing out of ordinary on accident year loss ratio; seasonal effect with Q1 typically higher than other quarters. High-value homeowners market experiencing increased competition; limits being offered lower so average premium dropping. On reinsurance: company evaluates retentions, limits annually; increased retentions many times over 17 years; 6/1 renewal date; can't commit to how treaties will be placed.

exchanges.question: How has competitive behavior changed over past six months from MGAs and admitted carriers? Submission growth flat quarter-over-quarter but down from year ago—demand driven or pullback on irrational pricing? Update on broker relationship expansion initiatives?
exchanges.answer: Competitive market across divisions; growth rate proxy for competition intensity. MGAs and new companies revving up on long-tail lines, specifically construction over last 4-5 months; premises liability and auto remain strong. Submissions ex-Commercial Property up 9% viewed as attractive; market reasonably steady and exciting growth prospects. Larger accounts under competitive stress have depressing near-term effect on growth rate; small to medium accounts still strong. Wholesale distribution model remains principal; company supportive of experienced broker teams starting new shops.

exchanges.question: Any change in retention, or is delta between gross premium and submission mostly pricing exposure and large commercial property mix? Small business E&S historically challenging—are larger competitors using technology to compete better with smaller customers?
exchanges.answer: New and renewal business hit ratios consistent quarter-to-quarter, no big change. Technology always huge priority for Kinsale since founding; expense ratio proxy for technology lead. Company can adapt new technologies faster due to skilled tech professionals and lack of legacy software decades old. Confident about adaptability.

exchanges.question: On property front, has pricing reset at lower level or continuing to drift downside? Using expense advantage to grow top line or already deployed? How equity portfolio performing?
exchanges.answer: No good news on property; easier comps in second half due to disproportionate commercial property volume in first six months. Company uses multiple advantages: accurate loss estimation, short/medium/long tail knowledge, expense advantage, underwriting advantage, analytics for risk segmentation, conservative reserving with 17-year favorable track record. Ambitious about growth but subordinate it to profitability. Gross written premium down 0.5% reflects large accounts stress and shift to smaller average premium. Equities performing well; 2/3 actively managed, 1/3 passive S&P 500; since late 2022 lagged S&P but matched Vanguard VYM benchmark; less tech weighting due to value orientation.

exchanges.question: Commercial property was $65 million Q1 versus $375 million last year—what portion in large property category? With capital coming in and going after lower returns, will ROE normalize back or need to come down to high teens long-term?
exchanges.answer: Commercial Property division average premium $30,000-$40,000 per policy; that division handles large shared and layered deals. Year or two ago average was north of $50,000; now either losing larger accounts or participating higher in schedule. With better underwriting model and significant cost advantage, confident in low 20s ROE, about 15 percentage points above risk-free rate.

exchanges.question: How does submission growth compare to overall market or E&S sub-segment where you compete? Where is macro trending and how are you running against it?
exchanges.answer: No specific information on overall market provided. Brokers canvass market for best terms and costs; assume some commonality between company stats and competitors' stats, but no definitive comparison available.

exchanges.question: On construction competition, seeing volume of opportunities? Any slowdown in construction activity? General casualty growth compared to fourth quarter? On cash flow, will it track with net written premium?
exchanges.answer: No delay in construction activity observed; company doesn't focus on large project-specific policies. Some areas experiencing delays but not where company focuses. Specific comparison stats not provided today, available in 10-K by division for three-year lookback. Cash flow expected to track with net written premium.
